headline: Deep learning and accelerated tools reshape genomic inference from raw sequencing reads
label: Deep Learning Genomic Inference
summary: Deep models now operate on raw reads and pileups rather than aggregated summaries, while mapping and single-cell tools push runtime and memory limits.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computation at the level of primary sequencing data, with attention to cost. SomatiX applies deep learning to allele-aware pileups from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA and is reported to outperform DeepSomatic. scRM pretrains a single-cell foundation model on scRNA-seq reads rather than count matrices and is reported as competitive. flashscenic accelerates SCENIC GRN inference on GPU, reporting 12-27x speedups over pySCENIC with r=0.9996 equivalence. brisc runs a multithreaded CPU workflow on 10M cells in 3 minutes. The arXiv workload characterization identifies memory-bound functions and cache behavior in DNA read mapping tools. What is new is the shift toward raw-read and pileup inputs, combined with explicit concern for throughput and memory behavior at scale. The items do not address a single biological question; they share methodological and systems concerns.
